item.title: Lindsay Clancy Murder Trial: Matt Walsh denounces her online defenders; jury remains deadlocked
item.description: In the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, jurors remain unable to agree on a verdict. Matt Walsh, a conservative commentator, has openly criticized defenses aimed at portraying Clancy as a devoted mother. He argues that her maternal instincts do not absolve her from criminal culpability. While prosecutors assert that Clancy's actions were intentional, her defense is focusing on claims of postpartum psychosis.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Streamer Eyes Twitch Switch: Clavicular says he has a deal; fans debate Kick future
item.description: Clavicular says he plans to start streaming on Twitch within about a week and claims he has a deal with the platform. His comments have divided fans, with some expecting trouble on Twitch and others questioning the deal itself. His Kick channel remains active, so it is still unclear whether Twitch will replace Kick or become another streaming platform for him.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Owens Questions Tpusa Direction: Clip attacks TPUSA’s new course; hints at rival conservative group
item.description: Candace Owens has sparked fresh controversy with comments about Turning Point USA’s future, suggesting that another organization could eventually rise and take its place. She argued that TPUSA has moved away from ideas she associates with Charlie Kirk and questioned its current direction. Owens also claimed Kirk would have wanted a different path, intensifying debate over his political legacy, TPUSA’s identity and the possibility of a new movement emerging.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Built in 1881 and closed in 2004, a $55 million Smithsonian building was chosen for...
item.description: The Smithsonian Board of Regents has officially selected the Arts and Industries Building as the site for the National Museum of the American Latino, concluding a prolonged discussion regarding its permanent home on the National Mall. Once renovated and modernized, this historic structure, which dates back to 1881, will eliminate the need for congressional approval for a new venue. Notably, the museum's first preview space already opened in 2022.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Hollywood actor Joel McCrea bought a California ranch in 1933; his family later donated 74 acres
item.description: The former ranch of Hollywood star Joel McCrea has been transformed into a haven for wildlife conservation. His family generously donated the estate to establish a wildlife sanctuary and parkland. The area is home to unique native flora and stunning rock formations. Additionally, the historic ranch structures were handed over to local park authorities for ongoing preservation, while educational initiatives and restoration projects thrive on this safeguarded land.

item.title: Florida couple spent 41 years preserving a 1908 house; it is now a local historic landmark
item.description: In Oneco, Florida, the Johnson Helm House has earned the title of the first local historic landmark in the county. Built in 1908, this charming residence has been lovingly preserved by Margi and Pat Nanney for over four decades, keeping its unique architectural attributes intact. Their commitment has prevented modern alterations from obscuring its character, while this recognition emphasizes the area's important agricultural history.

item.title: In 2008, Allen University moved a 1903 house and promised to restore it; now it is being demolished
item.description: A historic 1903 house in Columbia, South Carolina, is being demolished nearly 18 years after Allen University moved it two blocks and promised to restore it. The Robert Weston Mance House was linked to generations of Black community and civil rights leaders. After years of neglect, a legal fight over its future and concerns about safety, the city approved its demolition.

item.title: 40+ Tennessee Tiny-home owners sue over ‘zombie HOA’ they say developer still controls
item.description: More than 40 homeowners in Tennessee’s Sunset Bluff community have joined a $5 million lawsuit against developer Claude “Chip” Hayes III, accusing him of retaining control of their HOAs and mismanaging funds. Residents allege that nearly 80% of one HOA’s budget went to a lawn care company owned by Hayes, while several promised amenities remain unfinished.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Ingrid Alexandra: 22-year-old heir as King Haakon takes oath, future queen after 600 years
item.description: Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra, 22, has stepped into a historic new role as heir to Norway’s throne following King Haakon’s accession. As Haakon takes his constitutional oath, Ingrid Alexandra becomes the country’s first adult heir at the time of succession in modern history. If she becomes monarch, she could be Norway’s first reigning queen in over 600 years.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A Staten Island deli manager started paying kids for better report cards 3 years ago
item.description: A deli manager on Staten Island has sparked a remarkable movement by rewarding children for their academic achievements. This initiative has successfully gathered an impressive $500,000 to procure school supplies, benefiting numerous students. Thousands received fully stocked backpacks just in time for the new school year, showcasing how community backing can elevate a simple idea into a significant educational support system.

item.title: In 2023, buyers paid $87,000 for a crumbling 1979 Michigan concrete dome with caved-in ceilings
item.description: In Brighton, Michigan, a remarkable transformation has taken place with a once-neglected 1970s concrete dome home. Acquired in 2023 for $87,000, this property underwent a meticulous renovation, now boasting four bedrooms infused with modern luxury and eco-friendly features. Now on the market for $499,900, its unique design and energy-efficient qualities are captivating buyers in search of distinctive living spaces.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A 19-year-old's girlfriend fell onto train tracks; he jumped down to save her and died after...
item.description: A nineteen-year-old man lost his life in a tragic act of courage while on his first subway journey. He leaped onto the tracks after his girlfriend stumbled, attempting to save her. Unfortunately, he came into contact with the electric third rail. Now in critical condition, his girlfriend is hospitalized, spurring urgent calls for better safety measures on subway platforms.
